chargingModes.sae: Closest to unattended use of a household outlet without EVSE
chargingModes.interface: Standard household socket, no dedicated EVSE, no control pilot
chargingModes.home: Banned or strongly restricted in many countries (UK, US, IL; restricted in CH, DK, NO, DE). Not a home charging station.

chargingModes.sae: AC Level 1 (120 V) portable; also 240 V portable EVSE
chargingModes.interface: Household or industrial (IEC 60309 / NEMA) plug + in-cable IC-CPD (IEC 62752) + vehicle coupler
chargingModes.protection: IC-CPD: overcurrent, PE continuity, RCD, control pilot
chargingModes.home: Emergency / travel / temporary home charging. Daily use of household plugs is thermally limited (Schuko, BS 1363).

chargingModes.interface: Permanently connected EVSE (wallbox). Tethered vehicle connector or IEC 62196 socket-outlet. Control pilot PWM.
chargingModes.limits: 1φ up to 70 A / 250 V; 3φ up to 63 A / 480 V in the standard. Home practice: ≤ 32 A, ≤ 22 kW.
chargingModes.protection: EVSE RCD / RDC-DD, PE monitoring, interlocking, current coding via PP (Type 2)
chargingModes.home: The correct home charging station architecture worldwide.
Rare at dwellings; not covered in depth here.

pwm.description: IEC 61851-1 control-pilot PWM tells the vehicle the maximum current the EVSE will allow. The vehicle never draws more than this, and never more than its onboard charger.

dutyCycle.meaning: Available current I = duty × 0.6 A (for 10–85 % → 6–51 A)
